text:
Nina Patel: Ran an nsys capture on the 4-GPU dedicated cluster this morning. Timeline is weird — memcpy_h2d spikes on stream 2 and the batcher thread on CPU shows ~50-150ms scheduling gaps. dropping a small excerpt below and the command I used. :eyes:

Arjun Rao: can you paste the timeline snippet + kernel names? any signs of pageable fallback? :thinking:

Nina Patel: excerpt and kernel list pasted. kernel names: matmul_fwd_small, kvcache_lookup, prefetch_memcpy_h2d, matmul_fwd_big. Looks like a mix of many tiny kernels on GPU1 while memcpy dominates GPU0.

```text
NSYS TIMELINE (excerpt)
TIME ->
GPU0: [matmul_fwd_big][matmul_fwd_big]----[prefetch_memcpy_h2d: 28ms]----------[matmul_fwd_big]
GPU1: [prefetch_memcpy_h2d: 6ms][matmul_fwd_small][matmul_fwd_small][matmul_fwd_small]...
CPU: batcher-thread: blocked@12.342s -> woke@12.395s (sched latency ~53ms)
CPU: kvcache-worker: active during memcpy spikes
```

Nina Patel: capture command: 
```bash
nsys profile --sample=none -o /tmp/trace_3532 --trace=cpu,cuda,osrt ./run_infer.sh --config configs/dedicated-4gpu.json 
```

Sam: do we have metrics for pinned pool usage during this capture? pinned->pageable fallback would explain long hostcopy times.

Nina Patel: yep — pinned pool grows steadily then we hit a fallback event and hostcopy latency jumps. snippet: "pinned_allocated_mb: 1204 -> fallback_to_pageable: true @12.36s"

DevBot: deploybot: job/4221 trace uploaded: https://internal-blob/trace_3532.nsys (tag: prefetch-fallback)

Taylor W: sounds like two problems colliding: (1) batcher heuristic is emitting lots of tiny micro-batches causing kernel launch overhead and fragmentation, (2) prefetch is allocating many pinned buffers and we run out of the pinned pool -> pageable copies which are slower and serialize.

Luis Gomez: agree. try increasing prefetch_pinned_threshold or enable the new coalescing heuristic that merges tiny batches in the batcher. small config suggestion:
```json
{"batch_coalesce_ms": "3", "max_inflight_batches": "16", "prefetch_pinned_threshold_mb": "512"}
```

Arjun Rao: also add perfetto to capture thread wakeups. nsys shows CPU gaps but we need perfetto stacks to know if it's scheduler preemption vs voluntary yields. run: 
```bash
PERFETTO_OUTPUT=/tmp/pf.pb perfetto --config perfetto_cfg.pb -o $PERFETTO_OUTPUT &
nsys profile --sample=none -o /tmp/trace_pf --trace=cpu,cuda,osrt ./run_infer.sh ...
```

Sam: small kernels -> kernel selection path might be falling back to the "small-kernel" matmul due to quant path/tiling heuristics. any model-level changes in the rollout?

Nina Patel: we rolled a new quantized matmul patch two days ago (A/B canary on 10% traffic). I'll pin the old kernel selection and re-run capture with the coalesce/pinned threshold changes.

Taylor W: if you can repro, also capture nvtx markers around batcher queueing and kvcache prefetch calls. TX/rx timestamps will help correlate which hostcopy belongs to which request.

Nina Patel: will do. planning one more capture with: coalesce=3ms, prefetch_threshold=512MB, nvtx markers enabled, perfetto + nsys. I'll post the new trace link and short heatmap. thanks all :thumbsup:
